7. AMNIOCENTESIS & CVS:

•5% women require invasive Tests or 300,000/Anum.

 

Amniocentesis: Most common

-Early: Before 15weeks
1.7.1% loss rate
2.increased risk of talipes
3.Not recommended
-Late: After 15 weeks.
→0.5% loss rate.
-3rd trimester
→Not associated with early delivery
→Bloody tap 5 – 10%
→Repeat amnio 5%
→culture failure 9.7% =>more common.
→Indicated when late karyotyping is need

USG guided amniocentesis –

reduces bloody tapes from 2.4 – 0.8%.

Use 20G, 0.9mm needle.

Routes

•Extraplacental – preferable
•Transplacental – avoid – use only if no other option
•Go through thinnest portion.
-Difficulty anticipated
•Seek senior Advice who performs 100 procedures/year.

CVS:

• Loss rate more than Amniocentesis.
•Done at 10 – 13+6 weeks.
•Before 10 weeks – ed risk of:
-Limb reduction.
-Oromandibular Hypoplasia.
-Difficult to perform.
•Routes:
-Transvaginal operator choice
-Transabdominal able to experience

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Other risks associated with CVS and amniocentesis:

Consent: (written)

•Reason for procedure.
•Risk of pregnancy loss
•Accuracy & limitations.
•Culture failure.
•Reporting time.
•Need for Anti D.
•Medical Advice seeking after results.
•Long term sample storage.
•Type of cytogenetic risk.

Twins:

•By trained person who is experienced in performing selective termination.
•Loss rate 1%.
•Careful labeling of samples & Twins.
•Separate needles should be used.

Transmission of infection:

•USG probe in sterile bag.
•Virus screening should be done
•Viral load more reliable than antigen.
•Hep B & C => transmission limited data.
•HIV:
-Delay till viral load is undetectable
-Do if Pt is on HARRT & with low viral load.
-In 3rd more transmission risk.
-No t/m, 25% transmission,
-with t/m, 6.1% transmission.
•Use separate Gel.

Severe sepsis 1/100:

•Due to bowel puncture, skin contaminated, Gel or probe.
